claims.text: The solution-treated NbMoTaW reference alloy has a homogeneous BCC microstructure with no secondary precipitates.
Solution treatment at approximately 1600°C followed by aging at approximately 900°C for 1–2 hours will nucleate nanoscale Laves-phase precipitates in NbMoTaW.
The proposed aging treatment will produce a uniform precipitate distribution.
The aging-induced Laves phase will be ordered.
The Laves-phase precipitates will be embedded in a ductile BCC matrix.
Nanoscale Laves-phase precipitates impede dislocation glide.
Nanoscale Laves-phase precipitates impede dislocation source activation.
Impeded dislocation glide and source activation increase the yield strength of aged NbMoTaW.
The surrounding BCC matrix accommodates plastic deformation sufficiently to preserve or slightly improve plasticity after precipitation.
Relative to as-solutionized NbMoTaW, the aged alloy will have significantly greater yield strength.
Relative to as-solutionized NbMoTaW, the aged alloy will have significantly greater ultimate tensile strength.
Relative to as-solutionized NbMoTaW, the aged alloy will retain or modestly improve plastic strain to failure.
The proposed aging treatment will narrow the strength–ductility trade-off in NbMoTaW.
The predicted improvement requires the precipitates to remain nanoscale and uniformly distributed.
Precipitate coarsening or an inhomogeneous precipitate distribution may eliminate the predicted strength–plasticity benefit.
Overaging may compromise the ductility of NbMoTaW.
